title: M7.P1: Root-cause pass over the cloud epic before another cut — one folder model, proofs in the tree
body:
## M7.P1 execution update — 2026-10-03

The common migration layer now has strict complete-byte marker validation, numbered step1, retained original sources across pointer changes, failure-aware deletion/publication and a visible retry state (#356). Both settings-record race controls also fail before and pass after (#320). The focused runner now has93 passing cases; the complete host suite has1,367 PASS/0 FAIL/0 SKIP. #390 fixes marker test doubles exposed by the stricter production contract. Receipts: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-03-m7-p1/.

The table's appended execution update names T23 retry and T26 unsupported-marker controls. These do not complete the explicit actor × state/predecessor map. Next: finish that map and promote the new recovery scenarios into the candidate guest proof, preserving the actual RC2 compatibility boundary. Image criteria remain open; no new branded candidate exists.

## Current evidence and remaining coverage — 2026-10-02 (#385)

T01–T25, 72 focused host cases, source fixes and a promoted guest runner now exist (#383). Full host suite: 1,367 PASS/0 FAIL/0 SKIPPED before the dependency refresh. Classification cases do not prove every actor/transition. No new candidate guest run has occurred. The current acceptance map must include #356 future/malformed marker and interrupted tier/marker retry, provider failures, and the independently preserved settings/content dimensions. Review: docs/rasteratops/release-readiness.md.

## Readiness review update — 2026-10-02 (#375)

The D-WORKFLOW-134 analysis prerequisite is now documented in `docs/rasteratops/cloud-folder-state-table.md` (T01–T25, all seven actors) and `docs/retros/2026-10-02-cloud-runs-95-101.md`. The table records existing disagreements rather than silently deciding new behavior. Whole-boot T08/T11/T12, empty legacy alongside populated earlier/fleet folders, provider failure during settle, and worker-finished/card-visible must be covered before another folder fix is qualified. Promote the guest proof with per-case reset, byte/pointer/outcome assertions and an injected failure that exits nonzero. Existing suite passed 1365 checks but does not cover these seams. #377 tracks the reproduced failed-bucket-listing case. Executable cell coverage and proof promotion remain open.

## The maintainer's words (2026-10-02, during run 101's chain)

> Have we taken a step back to examine the workflows and the issues to look for broader patterns? I don't want us chasing our tails or over-optimizing smaller fixes when not doing root cause analysis.

## What exists today

Not a cross-cutting look. Each defect got its own code trace, blindspot or friction line. The last look across the work was the futro of 2026-10-01, which looked forward, and the last retro was on 2026-09-28. Since 2026-09-30 the cloud epic (#354) has taken 17 cloud decisions (D-CLOUD-156 to 172) and six kept cuts in nine hours (runs 96 to 101, 2026-10-01 15:42 to 2026-10-02 00:57 UTC). Each cut found a new case and was fixed locally, and the next cut found the knock-on:

- run 99: a fresh device beside an earlier folder holding the saves needed a join (D-CLOUD-169);
- run 99 also measured the follow check's cost, so the check became a setup step (D-CLOUD-170, run 100);
- run 100's proof found the backup making the stock `/GAMES` while the restore half said there was no folder (D-CLOUD-172, #364, run 101);
- run 101: D-CLOUD-172 broke vm-qa's round-trip suite, which backs up into a freshly reset `/GAMES` (0 of 9 files sent), and the pair test's step 5m, which expected the old behaviour.

**Pattern 1, one question decided in seven places.** "Where are this device's saves, and may this actor make that folder?" is answered separately by:

1. the wizard's seeding and `--settle`;
2. the transfer pages' scan;
3. the boot step;
4. the startup sync's restore half;
5. its backup half;
6. the exit sync;
7. the save rows.

No written model says what each actor does in each combination of the conf's folder and the cloud's contents. The cases are being found one build at a time.

**Pattern 2, the proofs that gate a candidate live outside the tree.** Guest d's proof is a session script copied forward each run. Its defects surfaced one per run:

- case D's remembered picks failed twice, and the first time it was rerun alone instead of fixed;
- the script exited 0 over two FAILs;
- the frame-diff claims were a pixel short;
- the fixtures named the old folders (blindspot 71);
- time-to-play's conf copy failed silently, and was first misdiagnosed as a slow probe (blindspot 64's shape).

**Pattern 3, the loop rewards local patches.** Each cut costs a build plus about 90 minutes of proofs. A found defect becomes a fix, records and a new cut, so the next failure is found before anyone asks what produced the last one.

## Decided prerequisite (D-WORKFLOW-134)

- No further cut of the epic until the folder model below exists. Run 101 stands as evidence.
- A state table for the cloud folder: the conf's folder state against the cloud's state, giving what each of the seven actors does. Reviewed before code, possibly by the council, then one classifier the scripts share and one suite case per cell.
- Guest d's proof promoted into the tree as a tool, with state reset per case and an exit code that fails on any FAIL.
- The mini-retro over runs 95 to 101, by the multi-pass process (#314's pattern), to find what this list misses.

## Can this be done on the VM?

**Yes.** The table's cells are the suite's sandbox and guest d; nothing here needs a device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/` carries the cloud folder's state table: each combination of conf state and cloud state, with what each actor does and the code line that does it. A walk of the table against the scripts lists no cell where two actors disagree, or names each disagreement as a decision.
- [ ] An actor × state coverage map names an executable assertion for every applicable T01–T25 cell (and a reason for each inapplicable one); `tools/last-good-scripts-test` runs those cases and passes. The previous commit fails the cases for the cells this work changed.
- [ ] The guest-d proof runs from `tools/` with a per-case state reset. Its exit code is non-zero when any check fails, seen once on a constructed failure.
- [ ] The retro file over runs 95 to 101 names each pattern with its guard, in `tools/`, `.githooks/` or `.claude/rules/`, as `ceremonies.md` asks of a blindspot.

## Verified independent-review additions (2026-10-02, #375)

Both Fable passes are complete and identity/digest verified. The primary retained full production-script host probes; these are not VM qualification.

- Existing T17 is now reproduced: cloud_setup with settlement rc124 or1 still exits0 and writes GAMES/README.txt; successful settlement control creates only the current layout. Keep D-CLOUD-171’s last-page continuation, but prevent seeding a superseded root whose settlement could not answer. Evidence: reviewer-settle-probe.{sh,log} in the #375 audit folder. This remains this issue’s existing failure/seeding work, not a duplicate finding issue.
- #379: settings-only old Backups must remain discoverable across pointer-only follow/settle; --apply already has a copying path and must not be conflated with those calls.
- #380: explicit empty CONTENT_REMOTE is a chosen cloud root to seeding and an unset value to migration; the missing-key/explicit-empty cases need separate fixtures.
- #381: the scan misses the writer’s per-device archive directories; use a real production upload as the fixture.
- Residual verification cells: two populated old roots on a lone device (configured-first remains the documented rule); unmarked current Content conflicting with an interrupted move/marker publication; restricted bucket-list permissions; timeout/cancellation between pointer writes. These are not reproduced product failures yet.
- The 59ms benchmark is guest-d execution on run101 with five samples per root, observed by a host driver. Fable’s host-only label and demand for a handheld number do not override VM-first policy.

- [ ] T17 fault-and-recovery VM case proves no misleading old-root seeding after failed settlement while the wizard can finish and the boot step can retry; retained log shows initial/final pointers, README locations and sentinel hashes.
- [ ] The new independent settings/content/archive dimensions and residual cases are represented in the table and promoted guest proof with reset, failing negative control and byte/pointer assertions; source-only hypotheses remain explicitly distinguished from executed failures.
